result:
I've made the fix in `repo/`. The two reported cases now come out right: 0.01 × 100 at 20% gives tax 0.20 and a total of 1.20, and no basket total has more than two decimals.

**On the draft:** I used its direction but not as written, because it misses two things.
- **`quantize` doesn't round half-up.** Without a rounding argument it uses the context default, which is `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`. Django also rounds half-even when it saves a value with more decimals to a 2-decimal field, and so does Babel, which the `currency` template filter uses to display money. So every rounding point now says half-up explicitly.
- **Rounding only `_get_total` breaks the "parts add up" rule.** Line amounts would still have 4 decimals, and the 2-decimal figures shown for each line would no longer add up to the rounded total. So I round at the line instead, and the basket total just adds up rounded lines.

**What changed:**
- **Tax and unit prices (`partner/strategy.py`):** `FixedRateTax.exponent` is now 4 decimals, and both `quantize` calls round half-up. Your 17.5% subclasses get this automatically.
- **Basket lines and totals (`basket/abstract_models.py`):**
  - Line prices before and after discount are rounded half-up to 2 decimals. Line tax is incl minus excl, so the three always reconcile.
  - The discount is rounded first and then subtracted, so 30.5745 becomes 30.57.
  - `_get_total` adds up rounded line amounts, so it also covers `total_discount`.
  - The unit prices stored on a line when a product is added are rounded half-up.
- **Order `LinePrice` rows (`get_price_breakdown`):** without a change, 100 × 0.012 would be stored as 100 × 0.01 = 1.00 while the line says 1.20. Payment and refund amounts are calculated from these rows. The leftover pennies are now spread over some units (20 × 0.02 + 80 × 0.01), so price × quantity always adds up to the line amount, both incl and excl tax. The return shape is unchanged; a line may just come back as up to three tuples.
- **Order creation (`order/utils.py`):** unit prices, shipping, surcharges and the total are rounded half-up before saving, not left to the database.
- **Order total (`checkout/calculators.py`):** shipping and each surcharge are rounded before being added, so the order total equals the sum of the parts as stored.
- **Display (`currency_filters.py`):** the `currency` filter now rounds half-up for every currency. Without this, a unit price of 0.7050 would display as £0.70.
- **Smaller fixes:** shipping excl-tax after a discount, the shipping percentage discount, and the percentage surcharge all round half-up now. I didn't touch the product promotion benefits.

**Existing data:** existing orders aren't changed and are never recalculated. Existing basket lines keep their stored prices. The "price has changed" warning now compares the rounded current price with the stored one. Without that, nearly every existing line would warn (11.9880 vs 11.99).

**Behaviour changes to expect:**
- **Line totals can differ from unit price × quantity.** 3 × 9.99 at 20% is now 35.96 (3 × 11.988), not 35.97, even though the unit price still shows 11.99. That's what keeping 4 decimals inside and rounding once means. It may be worth a heads-up to finance and customer service.
- **Some prices show a penny more.** Where the old half-even rounding rounded down (for example £0.60 at 17.5% was £0.70, now £0.71), existing baskets will show the "price increased" warning once.
- **Baskets frozen mid-payment at go-live** (e.g. a customer already at an external payment page) are recalculated with the new rules when the order is placed. That's the same as for any price change today. If such a basket included cases like those above, the order total can differ by a cent or so from what was sent to the payment provider. I didn't add special handling for this.

**Tests:** the command from the brief passes (189 passed, 1 skipped). Across all of `tests/` I got 1,644 passed and 9 failed. Two are category-slug tests and two are concurrency tests that hit SQLite "table is locked" errors. The other five are checkout thank-you and dashboard order-page tests that pass when their files are run alone. I had no unmodified copy of the repo, so I couldn't confirm they also fail without my changes, but none of them touches amounts.

I also ran some throwaway scenario checks: both reported cases, a 17.5% item, an existing basket line, and a full order with a 15% promotion where the order's stored line prices add up to its lines and total. In the repo's test settings promotions are applied excluding tax, so the 15% case ran on that path. The including-tax path (30.57) I worked through by hand but didn't run. I didn't add these checks to the repo.
